column2: Fever, wounds or rashes on the back, recent fractures, severe or radiating pain, pregnancy (in any trimester), severe osteoporosis; no pressure on the spine, kidneys or ribs. Cancer with bone involvement or night-time bone pain: do not press on the spine, ribs or pelvis; new bone pain requires a medical check-up.

Fever, wounds or rashes on the back, recent fractures, severe or radiating pain, pregnancy (in any trimester), severe osteoporosis; no pressure on the spine, kidneys or ribs. Cancer with bone involvement or night-time bone pain: do not press on the spine, ribs or pelvis; new bone pain requires a medical check-up. Agree on a stop signal (the word “stop” or a raised hand) before you start; the person giving the massage asks every 1–2 minutes “how is the pressure?” (target: 4–6 out of 10), and the recipient can ask for lighter, firmer or stopping at any time, without explanation. On request, or at sharp pain, numbness or dizziness, you stop immediately. In pregnancy, do not do this sequence (the prone position and the lumbosacral area — BL25, BL26, GB30 — are to be avoided).

Fever, pregnancy (skip the abdomen step), right after a meal, wounds, severe varicose veins, thrombosis. Do each step without rushing; if time is short, skip the abdomen or leg steps. In pregnancy skip the abdomen steps (CV12, ST25), the lumbar area (BL25, BL26), the ankle and foot (SP6, LR3) and the points LI4, GB21; ask your doctor for approval. Stop the sequence at sharp pain, numbness or dizziness.
No needles without the doctor’s approval; light pressure only (maximum 3 out of 10), no ball or forearm, 20–30 s per point; stop if bruising appears.

No pressure on the sciatic nerve if tingling or numbness appears. In pregnancy only gently, with the doctor’s approval. Do not do the exercise if you have a prosthesis, hip pain, severe osteoporosis or balance problems; stop at tingling or pain that travels down the leg.
No strong pressure in case of carpal tunnel syndrome or inflammation. In pregnancy ask your doctor before PC6. Chest pain, strong palpitations or fainting: stop and call 112.

GV16 is a sensitive area: no strong pressure, no twisting movements of the neck. Stop at dizziness, tingling in the arms or sharp pain. Pressure goes on the muscle, not deep, without tilting the head back. If dizziness, double vision, slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, weakness in one arm or new, intense pain in the back of the neck appears, stop and call 112.

You take anticoagulants or have a clotting disorder: light pressure only (maximum 3 out of 10), no ball or forearm, 20–30 s per point; stop if bruising appears. Ask your doctor.

Right after intense exertion, fever, feeling unwell, dizziness; if the energy wakes you up, shorten the sequence. Keep the pressure light (2–3 out of 10) and the lighting dim. If insomnia lasts more than 3 weeks, seek a medical check-up. In pregnancy skip the ankle point (KI3) and ask your doctor for approval. If you have thoughts of harming yourself or of not living anymore, call 112; do not stay alone.

Infection or wounds on the face, fever, glaucoma, recent eye surgery, contact lenses in place (remove them first), intense pain in the eye or teeth, recent facial trauma, recent cosmetic treatments. Never press on the eyeball and do not press if pain appears. In pregnancy ask your doctor for approval; the sequence contains no points marked “Avoid in pregnancy”.

Acute inflammation, swelling or severe pain at the wrist, recent fractures, persistent numbness of the fingers. Arm with lymphedema, with excised axillary lymph nodes or irradiated, with a dialysis fistula, catheter or port: do not massage without the doctor’s approval.

Acute inflammation, swelling or severe pain at the wrist, recent fractures, persistent numbness of the fingers. Arm with lymphedema, with excised axillary lymph nodes or irradiated, with a dialysis fistula, catheter or port: do not massage without the doctor’s approval. Do the sequence on both hands. Tingling or numbness in the fingers: stop and seek medical advice. In pregnancy skip LI4 (step 5) and ask your doctor for approval.

Intensity: a comfortable, dull or warm pressure sensation, never sharp or radiating with tingling; roughly 4–6 out of 10 (lighter on the abdomen, eyes, sternum and temples; for frail elderly people and children, maximum 3 out of 10).

LI4 is skipped in pregnancy. No strong pressure in case of edema or thrombosis of the arm. Arm with lymphedema, with excised axillary lymph nodes or irradiated, with a dialysis fistula, catheter or port: do not massage without the doctor’s approval.

Slowly massage the base of the skull (GB20) with your thumbs, then the temples. Skip LI4 in pregnancy. Sudden, severe headache with fever and neck stiffness, weakness or vision/speech disturbances, or occurring after trauma: emergency, not acupressure. If you are over 50 and the headache is new, with tenderness when the temple or scalp is touched, pain when chewing or vision disturbances, do not do acupressure: seek a medical evaluation the same day.

Do not press in case of recent trauma, dislocation or intense night-time shoulder pain. If you feel stinging, reduce the pressure. Arm with lymphedema, with excised axillary lymph nodes or irradiated, with a dialysis fistula, catheter or port: do not massage without the doctor’s approval.
You have not completed your safety profile.
A swollen, warm, red and painful calf or arm, on one side only (especially after a long trip, immobilization, surgery or during pregnancy)

Skip the card if you have kidney disease, kidney stones, lumbar pain with fever or blood in the urine. In pregnancy do not lie on your stomach; use the side-lying position and gentle pressure. Avoid the sacral area and direct pressure on the spine. Cancer with bone involvement or night-time bone pain: do not press on the spine, ribs or pelvis; new bone pain requires a medical check-up.

The partner places the thumbs on BL23, on the muscles beside the spine, at waist level, and on BL52, 3 cun lateral. Press simultaneously with light to medium pressure (3–5/10), without pushing deep, 30–45 seconds on each side, only on the muscle beside the spine, no strikes and no pressure on the flanks or ribs. Breathe slowly together. Before you start, agree on a stop signal (“stop” or a raised hand). The person pressing asks “how is the pressure?” at the start and every 15–20 seconds (target: 3–5 out of 10); the person being massaged can ask for lighter, firmer or stopping at any time, without explanation.

The partner places a thumb on PC6, 3 finger widths (approx. 2 cun) above the wrist crease, between the two tendons, and the other hand on ST36, below the kneecap, lateral to the tibia. Press simultaneously, with comfortable medium pressure (4–6/10; gentler on PC6), 60–90 seconds, while breathing slowly. Before you start, agree on a stop signal (“stop” or a raised hand). The person pressing asks “how is the pressure?” at the start and every 15–20 seconds (target: 4–6 out of 10); the person being massaged can ask for lighter, firmer or stopping at any time, without explanation.

The partner places one thumb on LU9, in the wrist crease on the thumb side, where the pulse can be felt, and the other on HT7, in the crease, on the little-finger side. Press simultaneously, with pressure so light that the pulse remains felt under the finger (maximum 4–6/10), and breathe slowly together. Before you start, agree on a stop signal (“stop” or a raised hand). The person pressing asks “how is the pressure?” at the start and every 15–20 seconds (target: 4–6 out of 10); the person being massaged can ask for lighter, firmer or stopping at any time, without explanation.

On LU9 the pressure stays light (radial artery). Do not press hard if you have vascular conditions of the hand or take anticoagulants. Arm with lymphedema, with excised axillary lymph nodes or irradiated, with a dialysis fistula, catheter or port: do not massage without the doctor’s approval.

On the temples the pressure stays gentle (temporal artery). If the pain is new, throbbing, with vision disturbances or occurred after trauma, do not do acupressure and seek a medical check-up. If you are over 50 and the headache is new, with tenderness when the temple or scalp is touched, pain when chewing or vision disturbances, do not do acupressure: seek a medical evaluation the same day.
It may give a momentary energized sensation in the large muscles; traditionally it is used as a “wake-up” before exertion or in the morning.
It may give a sensation of skin that is less “stuck”; it can be used as a warm-up or for areas where the skin feels “stuck”.

Gentle pressure, without pain. Insomnia persisting over 3 weeks, snoring with breathing pauses or a depressed mood require a medical check-up. If you have thoughts of harming yourself or of not living anymore, call 112; do not stay alone.

Moderate pressure, without sharp pain. In case of acute inflammation of the elbow or loss of strength, seek a medical check-up. Arm with lymphedema, with excised axillary lymph nodes or irradiated, with a dialysis fistula, catheter or port: do not massage without the doctor’s approval.

Light pressure on the temple. With epilepsy or a history of seizures, do not do repeated rhythmic presses on the head. If you have a new, severe headache, skip it. The stimulating effect may disturb sleep if done in the evening. If you are over 50 and the headache is new, with tenderness when the temple or scalp is touched, pain when chewing or vision disturbances, do not do acupressure: seek a medical evaluation the same day.

Pressure goes only on the bone above and below the eyes, never in the inner corner or on the globe. Very gentle pressure on the bone around the orbit; do not press the eyeball and do not apply pressure if you wear contact lenses, have glaucoma, recent eye surgery or an eye infection. Take breaks to look into the distance (the 20-20-20 rule).

The pressure stays light; no pressing on the side of the neck. In pregnancy ask your doctor for approval; the sequence contains no points marked “Avoid in pregnancy”, but keep the pressure light. If you are over 50 and the headache is new, with tenderness when the temple or scalp is touched, pain when chewing or vision disturbances, do not do acupressure: seek a medical evaluation the same day.

Acupressure stimulates the same points as acupuncture, but through finger pressure, without needles and without piercing the skin. It is applied for 30–60 seconds, with comfortable pressure, never painful, while breathing slowly. It is the safest way to learn about the points, but it has rules: some points are avoided in pregnancy and there are situations in which you must see a doctor.
Acupressure is not a treatment. Call 112 or go to the nearest emergency room; do not stay alone and tell someone you trust.

The profile marks points, variants, combinations and massage sequences. In simple acupressure sessions, the safety gate only takes into account pregnancy, anticoagulants, cancer, circulation and foot sensitivity, and lymphedema; for any other situation checked, ask your doctor before pressing firmly.

Keep the pressure light (2–3 out of 10) and the lighting dim. If insomnia lasts more than 3 weeks, seek a medical check-up. In pregnancy skip the ankle point (KI3) and ask your doctor for approval. If you have thoughts of harming yourself or of not living anymore, call 112; do not stay alone.

Wound, infection or rash on the scalp, fever, sudden and severe headache, recent head trauma. The pressure stays light; no pressing on the side of the neck. In pregnancy ask your doctor for approval; the sequence contains no points marked “Avoid in pregnancy”, but keep the pressure light. If you are over 50 and the headache is new, with tenderness when the temple or scalp is touched, pain when chewing or vision disturbances, do not do acupressure: seek a medical evaluation the same day.

Slow breathing through the nose: 4 seconds in, 6 seconds out. The likely effect is relaxation; it does not replace treatment for persistent anxiety. Thoughts of harming yourself or of not living anymore: call 112; do not stay alone.

Wounds, fungal infections, infections or cracks on the sole, diabetes with neuropathy without medical approval, thrombosis, swollen foot. Do the sequence on both feet. Pressure of 4–6 out of 10. In pregnancy skip the ankle and foot points (KI3, BL60, LR3) and firm pressure on the feet; ask your doctor for approval.

Pregnancy, less than 1–2 hours after a meal, severe abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, recent abdominal surgery, abdominal or inguinal hernia, bleeding, heavy menstruation, cirrhosis or fluid in the abdomen, aortic aneurysm, stoma, acute inflammatory disease. Do not start if you have repeated vomiting, a swollen and hard abdomen, you do not pass gas or stool, you see blood in the stool or vomit, you have flank pain with fever or your period is late and pregnancy is not ruled out.

Pregnancy, less than 1–2 hours after a meal, severe abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, recent abdominal surgery, abdominal or inguinal hernia, bleeding, heavy menstruation, cirrhosis or fluid in the abdomen, aortic aneurysm, stoma, acute inflammatory disease. Do not start if you have repeated vomiting, a swollen and hard abdomen, you do not pass gas or stool, you see blood in the stool or vomit, you have flank pain with fever or your period is late and pregnancy is not ruled out. NOT in pregnancy (abdomen steps: CV12, ST25, CV6, CV4) and not right after a meal. The pressure stays very light; stop at pain or feeling unwell.
Sudden weakness of a limb, speech or vision disturbances, “the worst headache of your life”: emergency, not acupressure.
